title: Maximum Difference Between Adjacent Elements in a Circular Array
statement: Think of `nums` as a ring: every element neighbours the element after it, and the last element also neighbours the first one. Return the biggest value of `|a - b|` over all pairs `a`, `b` of neighbouring elements.
notes:
## Intuition

In a ring every element has exactly two neighbours, so there are only `n` neighbouring pairs: `(0, 1)`, `(1, 2)`, ..., `(n - 2, n - 1)` and the wrap-around pair `(n - 1, 0)`. Enumerating all of them and keeping the largest absolute difference is already optimal. The wrap-around pair is the one people forget, and it can be the answer.

## Approach

1. Start `best` at 0, the smallest difference possible.
2. For each index `i`, take its right neighbour `next = nums[(i + 1) % n]`; the `% n` turns index `n` back into 0, so the last element meets the first.
3. Update `best` with `|nums[i] - next|`.
4. Return `best` after the loop.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, 4]`, so `n = 3`.

- `i = 0`: `next = 2`, the difference is 1, `best = 1`.
- `i = 1`: `next = 4`, the difference is 2, `best = 2`.
- `i = 2`: `(2 + 1) % 3 = 0`, so `next = 1`, the difference is 3, `best = 3`.

The answer 3 comes from the wrap-around pair.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass visits each of the `n` pairs once.
- Space: O(1): only a few variables.

## Pitfalls

- Skipping the pair made by the last and first elements; Example 1 depends on it.
- Using the signed difference: when values go down, `nums[i] - next` is negative.
- With only two elements the wrap-around pair is the same pair again, which is harmless.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | number of elements |
| `best` | largest difference seen so far |
| `i` | index of the current element |
| `next` | the element after `nums[i]` around the ring |

narration.2: There are exactly n neighbouring pairs in the ring, one starting at each index.
narration.3: best starts at 0, the smallest difference possible.
narration.5: Visit every element once; each one pairs with the element after it.
narration.6: The % n wraps the last index back to 0, so the last element is paired with the first.
narration.7: Keep the larger of best and this pair's absolute difference.
narration.9: Every pair has been checked, including the wrap-around one; return the largest difference.
